THE FIRST FIXTURE THAT IS A PAGE RATHER THAN A PHOTO, and it broke the header crop. Synthetic, so no personal data.

Same restaurant as fr-marche-ttc, with two CASE 1 happy-hour discounts. Ten items priced 158,90 before discounts; 'Happy Hour -50%' takes 8,50 off the Kir Royal (17,00 -> 8,50) and 7,00 off the Carafe (14,00 -> 7,00), giving the printed Sous-total and TOTAL TTC of 143,40. 'total' is 143,40, the sum AFTER the discounts.

TRAP 1 — THE CROP. The receipt sits in a wide blank A4 margin, so a quarter of the PICTURE was far more than a quarter of the RECEIPT. The cut landed four lines into the items and threw away Kir Royal, Salade and Soupe together with the first Happy Hour line, and the model never saw them: production returned 7 items summing to 121,30. Fixed by trimming the blank border before measuring the fraction. Verified locally: all eight photo fixtures come out byte-identical, only page-shaped images move.

TRAP 2 — THE DISCOUNTS, STILL UNFIXED ON PURPOSE. Expect 'total OFF' here: the scan returns 158,90, the pre-discount sum. Leave the expected total at the true 143,40 so the miss stays visible. A 'Happy Hour -50%' line is INDENTED under its item, and the MODIFIERS rules said indented lines are modifiers to ignore. Three runs in three at full resolution returned all ten items at full price, summing to 158,90 against a printed 143,40 — an overcharge of 15,50. A negative amount or discount wording now beats the indent.

TRAP 3 — THE DIRECTION. On a tighter crop the model saw the discount and applied it backwards: Kir Royal came back as total 17,00 with an invented originalTotal of 25,50, having ADDED the 8,50 instead of subtracting it. The printed amount on the item's own line is the price BEFORE the discount.

Tax is TTC, so taxAmount is null — see fr-marche-ttc for the full reasoning.

Quantities: Kir Royal x2, Café expresso x3, Crème brûlée x2. Each printed amount is the LINE total.

WHY THE DISCOUNT IS NOT FIXED (2026-09-23). Two prompt rules were tried and both failed. Telling the model that an indented discount is not a modifier did NOT recover the Happy Hour lines — three runs in three still returned 158,90 — and it BROKE English: en-caffe-caffe went from 2 items at 5.26 to 3 items at 10.31, returning the almond-milk modifier as its own item with the coffee's 5.05, stable over three runs. Measured side by side on the same photo: production 2 items/5.26, dev with the rule 3 items/10.31. The anti-drop wording written for discounts bled across into the modifier rules next to it. Both rules were reverted, so the prompt here is byte-identical to the one production runs. Do NOT reintroduce a discount rule inside the MODIFIERS section. The remaining failure is a reading problem, not a rule problem, and belongs with the vision-model work rather than with more prompt text.
